title: Pizza Fritta
subtitle: Neapolitan fried pizza with ricotta and black pepper
excerpt: Pizza fritta is a fried dough pocket filled with ricotta and black pepper. It is the street food version of pizza from post-war Naples, made at a time when wood-fired ovens were a luxury. The outside is blistered and golden from the oil; the inside is light and creamy.
sourceNotes: Pizza fritta emerged as common street food in Naples after World War II, when most families could not afford a wood-fired oven. The fried version uses the same dough as conventional pizza but is cooked in deep oil rather than baked. It is associated with the Quartieri Spagnoli neighbourhood of Naples, where vendors traditionally set up outside on the street. The dish features in the work of Eduardo De Filippo and other Neapolitan writers of the post-war period.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dough 24 hours ahead. Mix the filling just before frying. Eat pizza fritta immediately; it does not hold well.
recipe.temperatureNote: Oil temperature: 180°C for frying. Use a thermometer if you have one.

content.text: Pizza fritta is a fried pocket of pizza dough filled with ricotta and black pepper. It is Neapolitan street food, cooked in a pan of hot oil rather than baked in an oven. The outside blisters and turns golden; the inside is soft and creamy. It is one of the fastest things to make if you have dough in the fridge, and it is much better eaten standing up than plated.
You need four dough balls from the 24-hour pizza dough recipe. Have them rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.
Mix the ricotta, parmesan, black pepper, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl. Set aside.
Heat the sunflower oil in a large, deep pan to 180°C. If you do not have a thermometer, drop in a small piece of dough: it should sizzle and rise to the surface within a few seconds.

Stretch one dough ball into a rough oval about 20 cm long and 15 cm wide. Spoon 3 tablespoons of the ricotta filling onto one half of the oval, leaving a 2 cm border. Fold the other half over the filling and press the edges firmly to seal.
Lower the pizza fritta gently into the hot oil. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side, turning once, until deep golden all over. The pocket will puff and blister.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain briefly on kitchen paper. Eat immediately while crisp. Repeat with the remaining dough balls.

items.symptom: The pocket opens during frying and the filling spills out
items.cause: The edges were not pressed firmly enough before frying.
items.fix: Press the sealed edge with a fork or your fingers all the way around. The seal needs to hold against the pressure of steam building inside as it cooks.

items.symptom: The outside is golden but the dough inside is still doughy
items.cause: The oil was too hot and the outside cooked before the inside had time to set.
items.fix: Lower the oil temperature to 170°C and fry for a little longer. Medium heat is better than high heat for fried dough.

content.text: Pizza fritta is post-war Neapolitan street food. It was sold by women from large pans set up on pavements in the Quartieri Spagnoli when conventional ovens were too expensive to run. The dish has since been revived by several Naples-based pizzerias and is treated as part of the same culinary tradition as the baked version.
